Medicaid’s real problem isn’t just ineligible recipients—it’s systemic bloat. The House bill trims 7.6M from rolls but ignores the $715B in bureaucratic waste, hospital overcharges, and Pharma price-gouging baked into the system. Cutting coverage for immigrants and work-shy adults is low-hanging fruit, but where’s the audit of Medicare fraud or the $100M wasted on consultants to implement red tape?

D.C. loves performative cuts while leaving the real rot untouched. Until they slash the $500B in annual medical billing scams and bloated admin costs, this is just rearranging deck chairs on the Titanic.
